core1b.fresh_task: A convex spherical mirror has radius magnitude 48 cm. A real object is measured 72 cm from the virtual focus. A report says the virtual image is 8 cm from the pole. Construct a signed position-line with object, pole, image, focus and centre; calculate the correct image offset from focus and decide whether the report confused the two reference points.
core1b.protected_work: Convert measurements relative to focus and pole into one signed position-line representation and use it to identify inconsistent experimental claims.

stages.predict: Before solving, predict the outcome or relationship and record uncertainty.
stages.attempt: A convex spherical mirror has radius magnitude 48 cm. A real object is measured 72 cm from the virtual focus. A report says the virtual image is 8 cm from the pole. Construct a signed position-line with object, pole, image, focus and centre; calculate the correct image offset from focus and decide whether the report confused the two reference points.
stages.reconstruct: F=24, C=+48. y=72 implies u=−48. z=F²/y=576/72=8 cm from focus, so v=+16 cm from pole. Report's 8 cm is focus offset, not pole distance. Order O −48,P 0,I +16,F +24,C +48. Check 1/24=−1/48+1/16.
stages.diagnose: Only if your saved response exhibits this error: Using object-to-focus or image-to-focus magnitude as u or v without moving origin. Otherwise record insufficient evidence.
stages.repair: Draw all points in one fixed axis, then derive y=d+F,z=F−v before using Newton relation.
stages.boundary_test: For a finite real object, can the image lie beyond the convex mirror focus? Use the same position line.
